NASA’s Voyager 1—the farthest human-made object from Earth—briefly lost contact this month, then reconnected on its own.

The Deep Space Network missed the spacecraft during scheduled check-ins on October 18 and 19. Its signal returned on October 20, before engineers had sent any commands.

Early indications point to a failure in one thruster system, with the backup switching on automatically. Voyager’s fault-protection system puts the spacecraft into a stable mode while engineers investigate. The cause is still unknown.

In September, engineers completed an upgrade known as the “Big Bang,” replacing three heaters with more energy-efficient models. Voyager is powered by heat from decaying plutonium, and its available power drops by about 4 watts each year. The upgrade could help keep another science instrument running beyond the summer of 2027.
